[opaque block]

In brief, we are looking to engage with Tech companies to prevent and mitigate mass atrocities where 1) there are
upcoming Key Events that could create a risk of violence or mass atrocities, and 2) where tech platform engagement
could have a mitigating impact on those risks.
We (USAID and State) have been tasked by the WWhite House to separately prepare a list of up to five counties where
we believe the USG can engage with tech companies to mitigate risks of mass atrocities. We have been tasked to send
this list to the White House by COB on Tuesday 12/13. Both State and USAID pushed back that this is unreasonable,
but the deadline was set for us. After both State and USAID send their respective lists there will be another Sub-IPC to
crosswalk the two lists to create a final list of countries for inclusion.
As a group, the USAID representatives on the Sub-IPC came up with a short list of eight countries that we still need to
narrow down to five. At this point we want to make sure all the Regional Bureaus have eyes on this and can provide their
input, and ideally concurrence, prior to the Tuesday deadline.
The eight countries (in no particular order) are:
1. Burma
2. Bangladesh
3. Pakistan
4. Zimbabwe
5. Democratic Republic of Congo
6. Ethiopia
7. Mali
8. El Salvador

Hi everyone,
I had a talk with Garth who works with Vera, the Agency MDM lead and is coordinating the response to this
NSC request.
1. We both think it is a good opportunity to engage tech companies in addressing MDM ahead of
elections/critical events.
1. The term 'atrocity prevention' can sound shocking but the framework is similar to other
conflict/violence prevention frameworks including USAID's election security and election assessment
frameworks. Similar to the term anti-corruption, care has to be used when discussing the issue and
using the term with local partners.

Hello all,
Thanks to those that were able to respond, or shared your thoughts with those that responded. I hope that with this email I
can clarify some of the questions that have bubbled to the surface.
• I have been asked what my role is. I, along with Kim Brown, are the POCs for USAID on this sub-IPC. I am a
Democracy Officer on rotation with ITR. Vera Zakem asked me to cover this and report to her on progress. Kim
is a C3 that just came from the Tech company world and has incredible insights on how to engage with tech
companies. On the sub-IPC are a team of people from PPL, DDI/DRG, BHA and CPS.
[opaque block]

[opaque block] Google Vault - Sub-IPC on Tech/Atrocity Prevention/Key Events
• While Atrocity Prevention is the overarching theme of the Framework for engagement, it does not have to be
presented to host countries as an AP initiative or as an accusation to a country that the USG thinks they are at
the cusp of atrocities. The core of this framework is to put in place a process to coordinate Tech companies with
relevant USG Bureaus/Agencies/Departments in advance of a potential event to mitigate harm. This is an
opportunity to get the attention of tech companies.

case/proof of concept while watching the other four for possible engangement.

In brief, we are looking to engage with Tech companies to prevent and
mitigate mass atrocities where 1) there are upcoming Key Events that could
create a risk of violence or mass atrocities, and 2) where tech platform
engagement could have a mitigating impact on those risks.
We (USAID and State) have been tasked by the WWhite House to separately
prepare a list of up to five counties where we believe the USG can engage
with tech companies to mitigate risks of mass atrocities. We have been
tasked to send this list to the White House by COB on Tuesday 12/13.
Both State and USAID pushed back that this is unreasonable, but the deadline
was set for us. After both State and USAID send their respective lists there will
be another Sub-IPC to crosswalk the two lists to create a final list of countries
for inclusion.
As a group, the USAID representatives on the Sub-IPC came up with a short
list of eight countries that we still need to narrow down to five. At this point we
want to make sure all the Regional Bureaus have eyes on this and can
provide their input, and ideally concurrence, prior to the Tuesday deadline.
The eight countries (in no particular order) are:
1. Burma
2. Bangladesh
3. Pakistan
4. Zimbabwe
5. Democratic Republic of Congo
6. Ethiopia
7. Mali
8. El Salvador

In brief, we are looking to engage with Tech companies to prevent and mitigate mass
atrocities where 1) there are upcoming Key Events that could create a risk of violence or mass
atrocities, and 2) where tech platform engagement could have a mitigating impact on those risks.
We (USAID and State) have been tasked by the WWhite House to separately prepare a list of up
to five counties where we believe the USG can engage with tech companies to mitigate risks of
mass atrocities. We have been tasked to send this list to the White House by COB on
Tuesday 12/13. Both State and USAID pushed back that this is unreasonable, but the deadline
was set for us. After both State and USAID send their respective lists there will be another Sub-IPC
to crosswalk the two lists to create a final list of countries for inclusion.
As a group, the USAID representatives on the Sub-IPC came up with a short list of eight countries
that we still need to narrow down to five. At this point we want to make sure all the Regional
Bureaus have eyes on this and can provide their input, and ideally concurrence, prior to the
Tuesday deadline.
The eight countries (in no particular order) are:
